```{r 2}
query <- GDCquery(project = "TCGA-BRCA",
                  data.category = "DNA Methylation",
                  data.type = "Methylation Beta Value",
                  platform = "Illumina Human Methylation 450",
                  data.format = "Dataframe")
GDCdownload(
  query,
  method = "api",
  files.per.chunk = 10
)
methylation450 <- GDCprepare(query)
```


```{r}
methylation_clinical <- as.data.frame(methylation450@colData)
betas <- as.data.frame(methylation450@assays@data@listData) #takes a longer time
cpg_sites <- as.data.frame(methylation450@rowRanges@elementMetadata)

column_mask <- ifelse(colnames(methylation_clinical) %in% c('treatments', 'primary_site', 'disease_type','sites_of_involvement'), F, T)

methylation_clinical <- methylation_clinical[,column_mask]
write.csv(methylation_clinical, 'brca_methylation_clinical.csv')


site_mask <- !grepl('-', cpg_sites$gene) & !grepl(';', cpg_sites$gene) & !is.na(cpg_sites$gene) & complete.cases(betas)
betas <- betas[site_mask,]
cpg_sites <- cpg_sites[site_mask,]

write.csv(betas, 'brca_methylation_betas.csv') #takes a longer time
write.csv(cpg_sites, 'brca_cpg_sites.csv')
```


```{r}
methylation_clinical <- read.csv('brca_methylation_clinical.csv', row.names = 1)
betas <- read.csv('brca_methylation_betas.csv', row.names=1)
cpg_sites <- read.csv('brca_cpg_sites.csv', row.names = 1)
```


# Part 1
```{r}
# Keep metastatic and non-metastatic primary tumor samples
group_mask <- methylation_clinical$definition %in% c("Metastatic", "Primary solid Tumor") #instead of young/old mask like in demo

methylation_clinical <- methylation_clinical[group_mask,,drop = FALSE]
betas_clean <- betas[,group_mask,drop = FALSE]

# Check sample counts
table(methylation_clinical$definition)

# Primary solid Tumor is the base group;
# metastatic is the comparison group
methylation_clinical$metastatic <- methylation_clinical$definition == "Metastatic"

```


```{r}
#fitting linear models using a "target value"
mval <- t(apply(betas_clean, 1, function(x) log2(x/(1-x)))) 
#mvalue is another statistic for methylation, centered at 0 and ranges from -1 to 1
#this step will take a few seconds to run

design <- model.matrix(~ old, data = methylation_clinical)
fit <- lmFit(mval, design)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit)
```

```{r}
dat <- data.frame(foldchange = fit[["coefficients"]][,2], logPvalue =  -log10(p.adjust(fit2[["p.value"]][,2],method='BY')), geneName = cpg_sites$gene)
dat$threshold <- as.factor(abs(dat$foldchange) < 1)
```




```{r }
methylation_volcano <- ggplot(
  data = dat,
  aes(
    x = foldchange,
    y = logPvalue,
    color = threshold
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = .2, size = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 1,
    colour = "#990000",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = -1,
    colour = "#990000",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 2,
    colour = "#990000",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  xlab("Methylation Difference") +
  ylab("-log10 adjusted p value") +
  ggtitle(
    "Metastatic vs Primary Tumor BRCA Methylation"
  )

methylation_volcano

write.csv(dat,"methylation_results_metastatic.csv", row.names = TRUE)

ggsave(
  "/home1/jkjain/490_cluster/qbio_490_jennifer_jain/week08_methylation/figures/metastatic_methylation_volcano.png",
  plot = methylation_volcano,
  width = 9,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)
```
The volcano plot shows differences in methylation between metastatic and primary solid breast tumors. More CpG sites appear to have large negative methylation differences than large positive differences, which sugests that hypomethylation may be more common than hypermethylation in the metastatic samples. However, the metastatic group contains only 5 samples comapred with 793 primary tumor samples so the groups are very imbalanced, and the results may be sensitive to individual metastatic samples.
```{r }
# DESeq2 block, add genes names too
library(DESeq2)

# Keep metastatic and primary tumor samples
rna_mask <- rna_clinical$definition %in% c("Primary solid Tumor","Metastatic")

rna_clinical_de <- rna_clinical[rna_mask,,drop = FALSE]

rna_counts_de <- rna_counts[,rna_mask,drop = FALSE]

# Set primary tumor as the reference group
rna_clinical_de$definition <- factor(
  rna_clinical_de$definition,
  levels = c("Primary solid Tumor", "Metastatic")
)

table(rna_clinical_de$definition)

# Filter low-count genes
gene_mask <- rowSums(rna_counts_de) >= 1000
rna_counts_de <- rna_counts_de[gene_mask,,drop = FALSE]

# Make sure samples align
rna_clinical_de <- rna_clinical_de[colnames(rna_counts_de),,drop = FALSE]

# Convert to matrix
count_matrix <- as.matrix(rna_counts_de)
storage.mode(count_matrix) <- "integer"

# Run DESeq2
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = count_matrix,
  colData = rna_clinical_de,
  design = ~ definition
)

dds <- DESeq(dds)

de_results <- results(
  dds,
  contrast = c(
    "definition",
    "Metastatic",
    "Primary solid Tumor")
  )

de_results <- as.data.frame(de_results)




```
```{r }
# add gene names
de_results$gene_name <- rna_genes$gene_name[
  match(
  rownames(de_results),
    rna_genes$gene_id
  )
]
head(de_results)


```


```{r }

downregulated <- de_results$gene_name[
  !is.na(de_results$gene_name) &
  de_results$log2FoldChange < 0
]

hypermethylated <- dat$geneName[
  !is.na(dat$geneName) &
  dat$foldchange > 0.5 &
  dat$logPvalue > 2
]

interest_genes <- intersect(
  downregulated,
  hypermethylated
)

length(interest_genes)
interest_genes

```

```{r }
# define metastatic vs primary groups

# for methylation

methylation_metastatic_mask <- methylation_clinical$definition == "Metastatic"


```



```{r }

# extract PRSS23 RNA and methylation data
rna_primary <- as.numeric(rna_counts[gene_counts_mask, rna_primary_mask])

rna_metastatic <- as.numeric(rna_counts[ gene_counts_mask, rna_metastatic_mask])

# I used betas_clean: methylation matrix restricted to metastatic and primary tumor samples
methylation_primary <- betas_clean[gene_betas_mask, methylation_primary_mask,drop = FALSE]

methylation_metastatic <- betas_clean[gene_betas_mask, methylation_metastatic_mask,drop = FALSE]

```

The boxplot compares PRSS23 RNA exprssion between primary and metastatic tumors. The groups overlap substantially, and show no clear separation, which is consistent with a very small DEESeq2 log2 fold change of -0.040 (obtained below).

This plot compares average methylation at individual CpG sites within the gene PRSS23. The differences vary by CpG site and do not show uniform hypermethylation across the gene, which indicates that the methylation change is site-specific.

Final Explanation:
I selected PRSS23 because it showed lower RNA expression in metastatic tumors, and at least 1  CpG site with signfiicantly increased methylation in the metastatic group. however, the RNA-seq effects was very small (log2 fold change was -0.040) and the box plot shows no clear reduction in expression of PRSS23 in metastatic tumors. Methylation also varied greatly across CpG sites within PRSS23, as some sites showed increased methylation, some showed little change, and some showed decreased methylation. Therefore, the data and plots does not appear to provide strong evidence that increased PRSS23 methylation suppresses its transcription in metastatic breast cancer.
